name: pdfjs-dist
source: the npm registry tarball pdfjs-dist-6.5.438.tgz, unpacked; every file below is byte-identical to the file at its npm_path in its package's tarball, and keeps that path under the package/ directory

bundled.name: core-js
bundled.evidence: the core-js shared-store record in each legacy build file: version "3.51.0", mode "global"
bundled.source: the npm registry tarball core-js-3.51.0.tgz, checked against its dist.integrity; only package/LICENSE is taken
bundled.eval_note: each legacy file holds exactly one core-js global lookup, Function("return this")(), reached only where globalThis, window, self, global and this are all missing (never in a browser); the page policy has no 'unsafe-eval', so it would be refused anyway (tests/test_frontend.py allows that occurrence alone)

files.why: licence (MIT) of core-js 3.51.0, the polyfills both legacy build files bundle (each names that version in its core-js shared-store record); only the licence is taken from that package

the library, legacy build (display layer): loaded by the review page with import() when a document is viewed as a PDF; the legacy build carries core-js polyfills for the newest built-ins it calls, so it draws in older browsers than the modern build/ would
the library worker, legacy build (parsing, text content): started by pdf.min.mjs as a same-origin module worker
the ZapfDingbats standard font, likewise (check marks of form fields drawn on the page)

the Symbol standard font, which the library fetches when a document uses it without embedding it (system fonts stand in for the other standard fonts); the package has one standard_fonts/ folder, which the legacy build uses too
licence of the two standard fonts (BSD-3-Clause)
licence of the library wrapper of that decoder (Apache-2.0)
licence of the library wrapper of that decoder (BSD-2-Clause)
JBIG2 image decoder in plain JavaScript, imported by the worker for the same reason

JPEG 2000 image decoder in plain JavaScript, imported by the worker because the viewer runs with useWasm false (no WebAssembly, so no wasm-unsafe-eval in the policy); the package has one wasm/ folder, which the legacy build uses too

not_included: build/ (the modern build): it calls built-ins only the newest browsers have (Map and WeakMap getOrInsertComputed, Math.sumPrecise) with no polyfill; the legacy build polyfills them
legacy/build/pdf.mjs, legacy/build/pdf.worker.mjs and their source maps: the minified files are the same code
legacy/build/pdf.sandbox*.mjs and wasm/quickjs-eval.*: document scripting is never run
legacy/build/pdf.renderer*.mjs: pages are drawn on the main thread (disableWorkerRendering)
wasm/*.wasm and iccs/: no WebAssembly is used (useWasm false), so colour profiles fall back to the device colour spaces
cmaps/: predefined CJK character maps, which documents in English do not need

standard_fonts/ other than Symbol and ZapfDingbats: with useSystemFonts the library never fetches the other Type 1 fonts, and the four Liberation Sans files (GPL-2.0 with a font exception) are only its last url() source after the local() system fonts it names for the Helvetica family, so a computer with none of those draws such text in its generic sans-serif
web/, legacy/web/ (the full viewer and its stylesheet), image_decoders/, legacy/image_decoders/ and types/
core-js beyond its licence: its code is the part of the two legacy build files that the shared-store record names
